key_insight: A physics-grounded digital twin combines weld-pool modelling, AI surrogates and simulated robotic control to screen in-space welding conditions before experimental testing.
engineering_relevance: The framework could reduce process-development risk for robotic metal joining in orbital construction and repair.
method: Finite-volume thermal model captures phase change, effective thermocapillary transport and local pressure; gravity is assessed separately.
Gaussian-process and neural-network surrogates predict weld responses, with GP uncertainty estimates.
A simulated six-axis robot uses proportional control to adjust power-source settings as travel speed changes.
evidence_signal: GPs outperformed neural networks across all eight outputs in repeated five-fold cross-validation; finite-volume re-evaluation placed 12/12 closed-loop versus 9/12 open-loop points within an illustrative 1–3 mm root-side-width band.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based; thermal-vacuum, reduced-gravity and robotic hardware-in-the-loop tests are needed to assess model and controller validity.
paper_title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
